title: Privacy concerns put smart glasses under scrutiny as Norway seeks temporary ban
source_used: Road to VR (also Yahoo, citing ABC News)
key_facts: Norway's government announced (reported 7 Oct 2026) that it aims to introduce a temporary ban on smart glasses ("AI glasses") in selected public places, citing privacy.
The ban must still be put to parliament and approved, so its passage and scope are not certain.

Places under consideration include parks, beaches, museums, shopping malls, public events, spaces for children (schools, kindergartens, playgrounds, youth clubs), health institutions and gyms with changing rooms.
The government is not proposing an outright ban; the devices stay allowed in some places and for private use.
Minister Torgeir Micaelsen said the pause gives time for an investigation and informed debate to lay the ground for lasting regulation.
A special council will look at permanent national rules for wearable technology.
quote_evidence: The Norwegian government announced it’s aiming to introduce a temporary ban on smart glasses in a number of public locations, citing privacy as the main concern.

While the government says the temporary ban is a high priority, it must still be introduced as legislation and approved by Norway’s parliament, so its passage—and the scope of any eventual ban—aren’t yet certain.
why_it_matters_hint: A national government moving to restrict camera glasses in public shows rising privacy pushback against wearable AI.
